The file `/work/putnam_2012_b5.lean` now compiles with `lean` and produces no errors and no `sorry` warning. The only change is that the `sorry` is replaced by a tactic proof; the imports, statement, and `open` line are untouched.

The idea behind the proof: for each `x`, the supremum on the left is the supremum of the tangent lines of the functions `s ↦ g1(s)^x · g2(s)` at `x`. Each tangent line lies below its function, so it lies below the left-hand supremum. Taking the tangent point at `x` gives equality. To index these tangent lines by a single real `t`, the proof uses a bijection `ℝ ≃ ℝ × ℝ`, obtained from a cardinality argument. The functions are then `h1(t) = log(g1 s)·G` and `h2(t) = G − u·h1(t)`, where `(s, u) = σ(t)` and `G = exp(log(g1 s)·u + log(g2 s))`.

I removed the scratch files and the backup copy I made, so the only file left in `/work` is the solved one.
